title: Stabilize synthetic user profiles and golden-set comparator for perf regressions
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem:
Our perf regression suite shows non-deterministic percentile swings (p50/p95) across repeated runs. Root causes include highly variable synthetic user seeds, cross-test KV cache pollution, and a brittle pass/fail comparator that is sensitive to minor natural jitter. This makes triage noisy, increases CI flakiness, and slows down ship velocity for perf-related changes.

Goal:
1) Make synthetic load scenarios deterministic for a wide class of tests by introducing a small suite of deterministic 'user profiles' and stable seeding strategies.
2) Replace the current threshold-only comparator with a golden-set comparator that supports per-metric tolerances and annotated deltas, reducing false positives.
3) Add lightweight isolation shims to reduce KV and batching cross-talk between scenario runs.

Success metrics (measured over the next 6 weeks):
- Flaky perf-regression CI runs reduced from ~18% to <4% for nightly suite.
- Mean time-to-triage for perf alerts reduced by 40%.
- Signal-to-noise ratio on alert emails improved (fewer invalid regressions).

Approach and changes planned:
- Introduce 3 deterministic synthetic user profiles (short-chat, long-chat-with-attachments, streaming-sim) with locked RNG seeds and deterministic prompt templates.
- Implement a small deterministic seeding library that can be reused across loadgen clients (python and node runners) and documented in README.
- Build a golden-set comparator module that:
  * Stores canonical metrics per-scenario in a versioned artifact (JSON manifest).
  * Computes normalized deltas and annotates deltas with likely causes (sequence-length, batching rate, cache hit ratio).
  * Supports per-metric tolerances and an explicit allowlist for known noisy metrics.
- Add an optional isolation flag for the harness to reset in-memory KV caches and per-worker batch windows between scenarios. This will be gated behind a feature flag to measure overhead.
- Add unit and e2e tests for comparator logic and profile seeding.
- Provide migration guidance for existing scenarios and update CI job matrix to run both 'baseline' (fast) and 'stable' (deterministic golden set) variants.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Deterministic profiles may not capture full production variability; golden-set results must be used as an early-warning system, not the only arbiter.
- Isolation shims add runtime overhead; we will measure cost and gate by CI job.
- Storage of golden artifacts requires lifecycle and versioning policy; initial implementation will be in S3 under perf-artifacts with manual rollover.

Rollout plan:
1) Land deterministic seeding library and profile definitions (canary: 3 scenarios) — week 1.
2) Add comparator and storage of golden manifests — week 2.
3) Run both comparators for 2 weeks in parallel, collect FP/FN stats — week 3.
4) Flip stable comparator as primary for CI alerts if FP rate is reduced — week 4.
5) Expand to remaining scenarios and document migration — weeks 5-6.

Open decisions:
- Where to store golden manifests long-term (S3 vs internal blobstore vs Git LFS).
- Tolerance defaults per metric (start with p95: 5%, p50: 3%, throughput: 4%) — need PM sign-off.

Notes on observability and dashboards:
- Add a dedicated dashboard showing comparator deltas over time, per-scenario jitter, and CI flaky-run rate.
- Instrument comparator to emit structured diagnostic events for failed comparisons to facilitate triage.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic seed library available in both python and node loadgen clients
Three user profiles implemented and used by >= 30% of nightly scenarios
Golden-set comparator landed with per-metric tolerances and produces annotated diffs
Nightly CI flaky rate for perf suite reduced below 4% for two consecutive weeks
Runbook updated with migration steps and how to interpret comparator diffs
